findings.issue_text: Unconditional `updateMany` write added to the availability hot path: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` in CalendarService.ts now runs on every `getAvailability()` call not served by an early cache-hit return — every cache miss (which happens constantly since cache keys include date ranges) and, being placed outside the cache block, also when the cache path is skipped entirely (calendar-cache disabled). This causes write amplification and row locking on the app's highest-traffic path, and the WHERE on `selectedCalendar.credentialId` alone is not covered by the table's unique index, so at scale it is a scan plus a multi-row UPDATE per availability request.

The non-essential bookkeeping write is `await`ed inline in `getAvailability()`, so any DB contention/timeout/error in it fails the entire availability fetch even though the busy-time data was already fetched and cached — turning a non-essential write into a booking-page outage vector.

`data: {}` in the updateMany only works via Prisma's `@updatedAt` auto-injection and should be verified against the pinned Prisma version: if the engine ever rejects empty update data, every Google availability check breaks (P0 outcome).

'Delete cached data' is shown for credentials the user doesn't own, where the mutation can never succeed: the UI (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx) gates the action only on `hasCache` with no ownership test and deliberately renders it when `canDisconnect` is false, while the handler (deleteCache.handler.ts) requires `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id, userId: user.id } })`; team-installed Google credentials and delegated entries appear in every member's /settings/calendars list and produce cache rows keyed by that credential, so non-owning members (and potentially the whole team if team credentials have `userId: null`) see a menu item that always throws 'Credential not found or access denied' — a permanently broken action exposed to a large class of users.

Sentinel meaning change of `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`: previously it meant 'this row was last modified' (calendar toggled, channel id set, error recorded), but it now silently advances on every availability fetch; any existing or future consumer of `updatedAt` (sync/health checks, admin tooling, per-calendar or per-user freshness comparisons) now reads a churned 'everything is fresh' signal and will make wrong skip/re-sync decisions, leading to stale busy times.

The `updateMany({ where: { credentialId } })` in CalendarService.ts is over-broad: it has no userId scoping and doesn't intersect with the calendars actually included in the query, so one user's slot lookup bumps `SelectedCalendar` rows belonging to other team members and to calendars whose data was never fetched (and, depending on placement, bumps even when the subsequent fetch fails).

Broken error propagation in `deleteCacheHandler`: `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` conflates not-found and forbidden and surfaces to tRPC as a generic `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so platform/API clients can't distinguish the cases and every legit 'wrong user' click is logged as a server error (alert noise) instead of a 4xx `TRPCError` (`NOT_FOUND`/`UNAUTHORIZED`) as the rest of the codebase does; the client only ever sees the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast regardless of cause.

Migration backfills `updatedAt = NOW()` for every pre-existing `CalendarCache` row (including fully expired ones, since `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groupBy ignores `expiresAt`), so right after deploy users see 'Last updated: <now>' on caches whose data is old/expired and are invited to delete 'fresh' data — the exact freshness signal this feature ships.

Hardcoded "en-US" timestamp formatting in CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx: the displayed timestamp is always `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` while the surrounding strings are localized via `t(...)`, so all non-US users see US date/time formats inside a translated sentence; should use the locale from `useLocale()`.

`sed -i ''` in scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh is macOS-only and fails on GNU/Linux: GNU sed treats the empty string as the script and the real expression as a filename, so the substitution never runs and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is silently never updated while the script still prints '✅ Updated' — a silent wrong-success path.

P2: Unconditional DB write on the availability hot path — `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` in CalendarService.ts:1022-1023 is placed after the cache-miss block, so it runs on every `getAvailability` call including cache hits; since availability checks happen on public booking pages, every slot-fetch issues an UPDATE against `selectedCalendar` for all rows under the credential, causing per-request write amplification and row-lock contention (worst for delegation credentials shared across many users) — it belongs inside the cache-write branch.

The unconditional write changes the meaning of `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` to 'last availability check' rather than 'cache last updated', yet the UI's cache status is read from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (calendar-cache.repository.ts:172-187), so this touch does not even feed the feature it appears to support.
The update relies on Prisma bumping `@updatedAt` for an empty `data` payload in `updateMany` — this behavior needs verification against the pinned Prisma version.

P3: `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` in deleteCache.handler.ts:24-26 is not a TRPCError, so tRPC maps it to 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and masks the message in production, preventing the client from distinguishing not-found/denied from a real server fault — use `new TRPCError({ code: 'NOT_FOUND' })` (or FORBIDDEN) instead.

P3: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-29 and deleteCache.handler.ts:28-30 bypass the `ICalendarCacheRepository` abstraction/feature flag by going straight to the concrete Prisma layer (`new CalendarCacheRepository().getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)` and `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany(...)`); the mock returned when calendar-cache is disabled (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:26-30) is unreachable from the handler, so with the feature disabled these paths still hit the real table and mock-based tests never exercise this path — route both through the same repository/factory used by the rest of the cache code.

P3: Ownership semantics for delegated (org-managed) credentials need verification — CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:55,134 offers 'Delete cached data' for delegated connections (`delegationCredentialId` set), but the only server-side authz is `credential.userId === user.id`; if DelegationCredential-linked Credential rows are org-owned (`userId: null`), managed users will always hit the error toast (functional gap), and if they carry the managed user's id, managed users can wipe cache for a centrally managed connection — confirm whether org policy (`disableConnectionModification`) should gate this too.
P3: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:63 uses `sed -i '' -E`, which is BSD/macOS-only; on Linux (GNU sed) the in-place edit fails mid-script.
P3: The script's `cleanup` is only trapped on SIGINT/SIGTERM, not EXIT, so when the script fails the tunnelmole process is left orphaned with a public tunnel still open to the dev server.

SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId is called at the end of getAvailability (CalendarService.ts:1022-1024) outside the cache-miss branch, so every Google availability fetch — including requests served entirely from cache — performs an extra awaited DB write on the app's hottest read path: added latency, write QPS proportional to read QPS (the read-only path becomes read+write so it can't be served from a replica, adding WAL/autovacuum churn), and row-lock contention on the organizer's SelectedCalendar rows from concurrent slot-refreshes on popular booking links; it also updates all selected calendars under the credential rather than just the one checked, and the UI's 'last updated' comes from CalendarCache._max(updatedAt), not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so the write adds no visible value — it should be moved inside the cache-miss branch or debounced

The `data: {}` passed to updateManyByCredentialId relies on Prisma bumping @updatedAt on updateMany with an empty payload; if the model's updatedAt isn't @updatedAt (or the Prisma version doesn't touch timestamps with an empty payload), this is either a silent no-op or a thrown validation error that would break all Google availability fetches

deleteCacheHandler uses raw prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany and connectedCalendarsHandler hard-instantiates new CalendarCacheRepository(), bypassing the ICalendarCacheRepository abstraction/factory extended in this PR; under any non-prisma cache backend (Redis-backed/embedded) or when the calendar-cache feature is disabled, deleteMany affects 0 rows while the UI shows 'Cache deleted successfully', so the real cache persists until TTL and the user's intent to force fresh busy-times silently fails, causing stale availability and booking conflicts

deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } }) in deleteCache.handler.ts has no userId scoping, so deleting cache for a shared/delegated credential wipes CalendarCache rows cached for other org members, forcing a cold cache for all of them and triggering a burst of Google API calls and org-wide quota burn

The ownership check credential.findFirst({ where: { id, userId: user.id } }) will not match for members of a delegated credential, yet CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx now shows 'Delete cached data' for delegated creds (hasCache is independent of delegationCredentialId), so those users get an error toast on a UI action that shouldn't be offered, and the org owner can wipe everyone's cache with one click

The cache-status aggregate in calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-188 (groupBy with _max(updatedAt)) must read every CalendarCache row for the user's credentials since updatedAt is not in the PK index (heap fetches); the table has no TTL pruning in this code path — a new row is inserted per distinct availability window and expired rows are only removed on webhook invalidation — so the scan grows over time and expired rows still contribute to the misleading reported 'last updated' status

CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx hardcodes new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {...}) despite the component already having useLocale() available, so every non-US user sees a US-formatted 'Last updated' timestamp; the formatter is also re-instantiated on every render instead of using the locale hook and being memoized

The migration (20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9) backfills DEFAULT NOW() onto every pre-existing CalendarCache row, stamping them all with the migration time so the 'Cache last updated' indicator is meaningless (identical for all rows) until each row is naturally rewritten
scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses BSD/macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax; on GNU sed (Linux) the '' argument is treated as a filename and the script fails

[P2] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:70 computes hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt with no consideration of delegationCredentialId/disableConnectionModification flags, so delegated (org-managed) Google calendars with cache rows show a destructive 'Delete cached data' action, while deleteCache.handler.ts:17-22 authorizes via prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id, userId: user.id } }) — a plain-user ownership check that fails for delegation/team-owned credentials, producing a guaranteed 'access denied' error toast; either the UI must exclude delegated/managed credentials from hasCache or the handler needs caller-consideration for team/delegation credentials

[P2] packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-30 widens the shared exported UserWithCalendars type so allSelectedCalendars/userLevelSelectedCalendars now require updatedAt and googleChannelId in the Pick<>, a breaking signature change for every construction site, but the PR updates only one producer (packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:896-901); other call sites building the user shape with the old 3-field select will fail to compile or, worse, silently pass undefined for the new fields at runtime

[P3] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1024 calls updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data payload, relying on Prisma's version-dependent @updatedAt auto-touch; if it silently no-ops, the newly-required SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never reflects refreshes and consumers read stale values

[P3] CalendarService.ts:1022-1024 performs an unconditional write over every SelectedCalendar row under the credential (including event-type-scoped rows) on the availability-fetch path; it should be verified to run only on cache miss, not on every call

[P3] connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29 and deleteCache.handler.ts:28-30 import the concrete calendar-cache.repository module directly, bypassing the ICalendarCacheRepository abstraction and its disabled-mode mock selection (CalendarCacheRepositoryMock), so when calendar-cache is disabled these paths behave differently from every other call site in the codebase

[P3] deleteCache.handler.ts:28-30 uses raw prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany instead of deleteManyByCredential, skipping whatever invalidation/disabled-feature handling deleteManyByCredential is responsible for

[P3] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:90-93 hardcodes 'en-US' in new Intl.DateTimeFormat for the cache timestamp while the rest of the component uses useLocale(), so non-English users get US-formatted dates in an otherwise translated UI; the i18n locale should be passed to Intl.DateTimeFormat

[P3] SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:72-80,125-132 now always passes a truthy actions slot (a wrapper div that may render null) instead of only rendering actions when disconnection was allowed, so delegated/managed or non-Google calendar rows render an empty 8rem action area that didn't exist before — a layout/visual contract drift in a shared platform component consumed by embeds
[P3] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:66-67 uses BSD-only sed syntax (sed -i '' -E); GNU sed treats the empty-string suffix as an input filename and errors, so the script fails on Linux

[P3] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh sets ENV_FILE="../.env" resolved relative to the caller's CWD rather than the script's directory, so running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root writes the wrong .env file

[P3] CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:43-51 deleteCache mutation has no self-invalidation of viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (asymmetric with disconnectMutation, which invalidates in onSettled at lines 62-65) and relies entirely on the optional onSuccess prop, so consumers that don't pass a refetching onSuccess will keep showing the deleted cache's 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete option after a successful deletion

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1023: updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called with an empty update payload at the end of getAvailability; several Prisma versions reject empty `data` on updateMany with PrismaClientValidationError and this PR never adds @updatedAt to SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (only CalendarCache.updatedAt is annotated), so the call either throws on every Google Calendar availability fetch (P0-level failure), silently no-ops leaving consumers of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt with stale data, or works only if the repo's Prisma version auto-injects the timestamp.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1023: the cosmetic bookkeeping write is awaited inline with no try/catch in the highest-traffic path (getAvailability), so any transient DB error in this non-critical write fails the entire availability lookup — and it can throw after setAvailabilityInCache already succeeded, making the failure flaky and hard to diagnose.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1023: the unconditional multi-row UPDATE of all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential runs on every cache-expired availability check, causing write amplification and row-lock contention with webhook channel bookkeeping on the same rows.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:14-22: the only authorization path is prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id, userId: user.id } }), but delegation/org-managed credentials (which CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx deliberately renders cache-status/delete actions for, since CalendarCache.userId is nullable and cache rows exist for such credentials) are not owned via userId, so for exactly the users the UI targets the request always fails with 'Credential not found or access denied' — no one, not even an org admin, can clean delegated caches through this endpoint.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts: the authorization failure is thrown via `throw new Error(...)` instead of a TRPCError, so an expected authorization outcome is surfaced as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than a 4xx, which is noisy for 5xx-based alerting.
scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68: uses macOS/BSD-only sed syntax (`sed -i '' -E ...`); on Linux GNU sed the '' is parsed as an input filename and sed errors out.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh: the script has no `set -e` and unconditionally prints the '✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in ../.env' success message without checking sed's exit code, so when the sed edit fails the operator is told it succeeded while GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated, and subsequent webhook tests silently point at a stale/missing URL and just time out.

packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:33-40: deleteCacheMutation refreshes the UI only through the optional onSuccess prop and, unlike its sibling disconnectMutation (which invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and utils.viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled in the same file), has no built-in query invalidation, so any call site that forgets onSuccess keeps rendering a stale 'Cache Status / Delete cached data' menu until an unrelated refetch.

deleteCache handler rejects delegated credentials: it requires credential.userId === user.id, but delegation credentials are created with userId: null, so every org user with a delegated Google calendar who clicks the delete-cache action gets an 'Error deleting cache' toast — this primary flow for org-managed calendars is completely untested

No tests exist for the new destructive deleteCache mutation: cross-user credentialId rejection (IDOR via the findFirst({ id, userId }) guard), nonexistent credentialId rejection, and that the success path deletes only that credential's cache rows are all unverified
deleteCache.handler.ts throws a bare generic Error instead of TRPCError, so the client cannot distinguish 404/403 from 500

In getAvailability (CalendarService.ts:1022-1024), the new updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is placed outside the cache-miss if block, so it runs on every availability check — including cache hits — on the app's hottest path (booking page slot rendering)

The getAvailability write relies on undocumented Prisma behavior that an empty data: {} on updateMany triggers an @updatedAt bump to SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; if it is a no-op or validation error, the feature silently dies or availability checks break outright
In the delegated-credential case, the updateMany where: { credentialId } updates all org members' SelectedCalendar rows on every availability request, causing cross-user write amplification

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is only exercised via the mock (which returns []), never against a real database: the groupBy/_max semantics with multiple cache rows per credential, expired rows counting toward 'last updated', empty credentialIds input, and the null-mapping in connectedCalendars.handler.ts:33 are all unverified

connectedCalendars.handler.ts directly instantiates new CalendarCacheRepository() instead of going through the mock selection mechanism, and the new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds does not check the calendar-cache disabled flag (unlike its siblings); no test verifies connectedCalendars still works and returns cacheUpdatedAt: null when calendar-cache is disabled
deleteCache.handler.ts calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, bypassing CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential

The disconnect affordance was replaced by an untested CredentialActionsDropdown component (ellipsis dropdown, menu item, confirmation dialog), orphaning existing e2e/component coverage of the old disconnect flow and leaving the return null contract, cache-status visibility logic, and both confirm dialogs untested

deleteCacheMutation performs no tRPC invalidation (unlike disconnectMutation's onSettled invalidations), so UI refresh depends entirely on the onSuccess/onChanged callback; no test asserts that connectedCalendars refetches and cache status disappears after delete

CredentialActionsDropdown hardcodes 'en-US' in new Intl.DateTimeFormat despite using useLocale() for translations, forcing US date ordering and 12h clock on all users — a locale regression with no i18n test

The migration backfills legacy CalendarCache rows with updatedAt = NOW(), so users see a misleading 'Last updated' deploy-time timestamp for caches actually written days earlier; the intended behavior for legacy rows is unpinned by any test
scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh is named a test but has zero assertions and cannot run in CI, inflating apparent coverage for the webhook/cache-invalidation behavior this PR supports
scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses BSD/macOS-only sed -i '' -E syntax that errors on GNU sed (fails on Linux dev machines), and its ENV_FILE relative path is cwd-dependent

SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper now always renders an empty w-32 flex wrapper even when the dropdown returns null, leaving an empty right-hand gap for delegated non-Google calendars where nothing rendered before — an untested visual regression

Orphaned SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write on the availability hot path: updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) in CalendarService.ts passes an empty data object relying only on Prisma's implicit @updatedAt bump, but nothing in this PR reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (the UI's cache status comes from CalendarCache.updatedAt) — a parallel 'last updated' mechanism with the write side present and the read side missing

The empty-data updateManyByCredentialId call is placed outside the cache-miss block, so it fires on every availability check (even cache hits), adding a DB write to the hottest read path per credential; it should be removed if vestigial or moved inside the miss branch and actually consumed if intentional
updateManyByCredentialId exposes the full Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput when its only caller passes {} — a narrow touchByCredentialId() would make the intent explicit and not invite misuse

Dead type/select additions: updatedAt and googleChannelId are newly added to the UserWithCalendars picks and the user repository select, but no code in the change set consumes them (the wrapper only uses connectedCalendar.cacheUpdatedAt), forcing every implementer/test fixture constructing UserWithCalendars to carry two unused fields that future readers will assume are load-bearing

deleteCache.handler.ts bypasses the calendar-cache repository abstraction by calling prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } }) directly instead of the already-declared ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential, creating a second deletion path that duplicates the mock's disabled-cache semantics (raw delete still hits the table when the feature flag says cache is off) and is inconsistent with the read side of the same PR

connectedCalendars.handler.ts instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository directly with new CalendarCacheRepository(), hard-coupling the handler and bypassing the factory/selector used by other call sites, so when calendar-cache is disabled the handler queries the real table instead of taking the cheap mock path

CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx re-implements the disconnect flow instead of reusing DisconnectIntegration: it duplicates the viewer.credentials.delete mutation, confirmation dialog, success/error toasts, and query invalidation, creating two parallel implementations of 'remove a credential with confirm' that will drift

Provider-specific logic hard-coded inside a generically-named component: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx bakes 'only Google has a cache' into the client via isGoogleCalendar and hasCache checks, even though CalendarCache is provider-agnostic and the server already gates by data presence — a redundant coupling leak meaning the next provider that gets caching silently gets no cache UI
CredentialActionsDropdown accepts integrationType: string instead of the app-type union (App["type"]), accepting any string at the component boundary

Hard-coded Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) in CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx ignores the active locale from useLocale() and the app's shared localized date utilities, giving every non-en-US user a US-formatted date and setting a copy-paste precedent for future cache-status surfaces

Inconsistent cache-invalidation responsibility: disconnectMutation self-invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled, while deleteCacheMutation relies entirely on the optional onSuccess callback, so any caller that doesn't pass (or refetch in) onSuccess shows a stale 'last updated' timestamp after a successful delete

Duplicated input contract for deleteCache: the zod schema is defined inline in the router (the sibling procedure imports ZConnectedCalendarsInputSchema from a co-located .schema.ts) and the handler hand-rolls a DeleteCacheOptions type repeating credentialId: number — the same contract is maintained in two hand-written places that can drift

deleteCache.handler.ts throws a plain Error("Credential not found or access denied") instead of a TRPCError, surfacing to clients as a generic INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, conflating the not-found and unauthorized cases in one message, and deviating from the error-code convention used by sibling handlers

SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper always renders the flex w-32 justify-end actions container even when CredentialActionsDropdown returns null (delegated, non-Google credentials), leaving an empty 8rem spacer in the card header; null-handling lives inside the child while the layout container assumes it always renders

macOS-only BSD sed syntax in scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh: sed -i '' -E fails on GNU/Linux (and CI/dev containers) because '' is not consumed as the in-place suffix; the shared script needs a portable invocation (sed -i.bak + cleanup, or awk/perl) or platform detection
ENV_FILE="../.env" in scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh only works when the script is run from inside scripts/, which isn't enforced or documented

The migration (packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql) adds CalendarCache.updatedAt as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(); NOW() is a volatile function and thus ineligible for PostgreSQL 11+'s missing-value fast path (constant defaults only), so on any non-empty table Postgres falls back to a full table rewrite while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all availability/cache queries on this hot, populated table for the duration of the rewrite (deploy-time sitewide availability risk proportional to table size; safer pattern is nullable add, batched backfill, then SET DEFAULT NOW() and SET NOT NULL).

The migration backfill stamps every legacy CalendarCache row with the migration run time, which the new UI then reports as 'Last updated' — semantically wrong for stale entries until they are rewritten or purged.

CalendarService.ts calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) outside the cache-miss branch, so every getAvailability() call — including cache hits, which were previously read-only — issues an UPDATE setting updatedAt for all selected-calendar rows under the credential; for shared/team credentials every member's availability check rewrites every member's rows, causing row-lock contention and WAL/autovacuum churn on the hottest endpoint, and nothing in the PR consumes the written value (the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt).

The unconditional write silently repurposes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt from 'record last updated' to 'last availability fetch', and relies on the implicit Prisma behavior that empty data still sets @updatedAt.

CredentialActionsDropdown gates the 'Delete cached data' action only on isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt — not on ownership, delegationCredentialId, or disableConnectionModification the way 'Remove app' is gated — while the deleteCache handler requires credential.userId === user.id, so every non-owner member of org-installed/team credentials that have CalendarCache rows sees the action and always gets 'Error deleting cache', a dead-end UI.

deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } }) in deleteCache.handler.ts has no userId scoping, so when the owner deletes the cache it wipes cached rows for all team members, causing an org-wide cache-miss refill burst against the Google API.

CredentialActionsDropdown formats the 'Last updated' timestamp with a hardcoded new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { dateStyle: 'short', timeStyle: 'short' }) instead of the locale already provided by useLocale(), so non-US-locale users get US date/time ordering in an otherwise localized UI.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses BSD/macOS-only sed -i '' syntax; on GNU/Linux sed interprets '' as an (empty) script and the command errors out, leaving a broken env update after the tunnel is already up (dev-only tooling, but a real portability bug).

deleteCache handler bypasses the ICalendarCacheRepository abstraction by calling prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly instead of deleteManyByCredential, so with a Redis-backed repository active, Redis-resident cache entries survive deletion and stale data keeps being served while the user sees a 'Cache deleted successfully' toast (silent-pass), and the calendar-cache feature-disabled flag is ignored

connectedCalendars status handler instantiates the concrete new CalendarCacheRepository() instead of resolving it through the app's repository factory, leaving the newly added CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds method as unreachable dead code and allowing the 'Last updated' status to be read from the wrong backend (DB CalendarCache table instead of the active Redis cache), including still issuing a DB groupBy when calendar-cache is disabled

Unconditional SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write on the getAvailability hot path: the empty data {} relies on implicit Prisma @updatedAt injection (fragile, could silently become a no-op or throw), every availability check issues an O(org-size) UPDATE causing row-lock contention on delegation credentials, the write lacks try/catch error isolation so its failure fails the entire getAvailability call, nothing in the PR consumes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, and it is placed outside the fetch branch so updatedAt can be bumped without a fetch having occurred

deleteCache is an unthrottled authedProcedure that flushes all cache rows for a credential with no rate limiting or cooldown, so repeated deletion turns every incoming availability check into a cache miss and a burst of upstream Google API calls — a cheap self-inflicted DoS lever that burns Google API quota and degrades the user's own booking pages

deleteCache ownership check uses findFirst({ id, userId }) only, so team-owned credentials (userId null, teamId set) always fail — with a plain throw new Error misclassified as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, polluting error logs — while CredentialActionsDropdown offers the delete action without ownership awareness, promising an action that can never succeed

CredentialActionsDropdown hardcodes new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) when formatting cacheUpdatedAt, bypassing the app's locale (useLocale is available) and its date/timezone formatting utilities, so non-US users get US-formatted dates for a timestamp-centric feature

SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper now always renders the flex w-32 justify-end wrapper div even when CredentialActionsDropdown returns null, leaving an empty 128px spacer where the old code rendered nothing

In the second actions block of SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper, the new canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification condition additionally hides disconnect when disableConnectionModification is set, silently removing an action that was previously available there (undocumented behavior change)

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses macOS-only sed -i ''; on Linux/GNU sed the empty string is parsed as the script and the substitution expression as a filename, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL never gets rewritten yet the script still prints success and exits 0

The auto-generated warning comment in migration 20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql says the column was added without a default value (not possible if the table is not empty), but the SQL actually adds NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() — the stale comment misleads future maintainers and auditors scanning for risky migrations

In a tRPC mutation (`deleteCache` in `_router.tsx`), throwing a plain `Error` will typically be treated as an internal error by tRPC (i.e., not a typed/expected error with an explicit code like NOT_FOUND/UNAUTHORIZED), which can surface to clients as a generic INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and loses semantic distinction between not-found vs access-denied cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration (packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql) adds CalendarCache.updatedAt as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(); NOW() is a volatile function and thus ineligible for PostgreSQL 11+'s missing-value fast path (constant defaults only), so on any non-empty table Postgres falls back to a full table rewrite while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all availability/cache queries on this hot, populated table for the duration of the rewrite (deploy-time sitewide availability risk proportional to table size; safer pattern is nullable add, batched backfill, then SET DEFAULT NOW() and SET NOT NULL).

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly does `ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();`. A `DEFAULT now()` is not a constant default, so it will not use Postgres 11+ “fast default / missing value” optimization (which requires a constant default), meaning Postgres may rewrite the whole table and take an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock during the ALTER. That’s a deploy-time availability/perf risk rather than a functional correctness bug, but it is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The migration backfill stamps every legacy CalendarCache row with the migration run time, which the new UI then reports as 'Last updated' — semantically wrong for stale entries until they are rewritten or purged.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (migration.sql) and the schema sets `@default(now()) @updatedAt`. When this column is added, existing rows will be populated with the default timestamp at migration time, regardless of when the cache value was actually written. The new UI displays this value via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (max `updatedAt`) and `CredentialActionsDropdown` renders `t("cache_last_updated", { timestamp: ... cacheUpdatedAt })`, so legacy/stale cache entries will be reported as “Last updated” at the migration run time, which is semantically incorrect until rewritten/purged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) outside the cache-miss branch, so every getAvailability() call — including cache hits, which were previously read-only — issues an UPDATE setting updatedAt for all selected-calendar rows under the credential; for shared/team credentials every member's availability check rewrites every member's rows, causing row-lock contention and WAL/autovacuum churn on the hottest endpoint, and nothing in the PR consumes the written value (the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an unconditional call added in `CalendarService.ts`: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` placed after the cache-miss logic, so it will run on every `getAvailability()` execution (cache hit or miss). That introduces a write-path DB operation on what was otherwise read-only for cache hits, which plausibly creates avoidable load/lock/WAL churn on a hot endpoint. However, the finding’s claim that it “issues an UPDATE setting updatedAt” is not strictly verifiable from the diff because the call passes an empty `data: {}` (it’s unclear whether Prisma treats that as a no-op, bumps `@updatedAt`, or errors). The point that the PR’s UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`) is supported by the diff, making the added update look unused in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unconditional write silently repurposes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt from 'record last updated' to 'last availability fetch', and relies on the implicit Prisma behavior that empty data still sets @updatedAt.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional call after availability fetch: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` with a comment explicitly stating it is meant to "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt". This effectively uses `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` as a signal for “last availability fetch” rather than “last record change”, which is a semantic/architecture concern. It also implicitly depends on Prisma behavior that an updateMany with empty `data: {}` will still touch the `@updatedAt` field—something not guaranteed by the diff itself and potentially fragile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown gates the 'Delete cached data' action only on isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt — not on ownership, delegationCredentialId, or disableConnectionModification the way 'Remove app' is gated — while the deleteCache handler requires credential.userId === user.id, so every non-owner member of org-installed/team credentials that have CalendarCache rows sees the action and always gets 'Error deleting cache', a dead-end UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the cache delete UI is shown whenever `hasCache` is true (`const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;`), regardless of `delegationCredentialId` or `disableConnectionModification` (which are only used to gate `canDisconnect`). So delegation/locked credentials can still show “Delete cached data” and allow clicking it. However, the TRPC handler `deleteCache.handler.ts` authorizes strictly by `credential.userId === user.id` (`findFirst` with `{ id: credentialId, userId: user.id }`) and otherwise throws, producing the toast error path in the UI (`onError: showToast(t("error_deleting_cache"))`). This creates a verifiable dead-end behavior for any connected calendar entries where the viewer isn’t the credential owner (or where disconnect is intentionally disabled via delegation/flags) but cache rows exist (cache status is computed for all `connectedCalendars` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } }) in deleteCache.handler.ts has no userId scoping, so when the owner deletes the cache it wipes cached rows for all team members, causing an org-wide cache-miss refill burst against the Google API.

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler first verifies ownership by fetching the `credential` with `where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }`. The subsequent `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` therefore deletes cache entries for that specific credential ID. The diff does not show any mechanism where multiple team members would share the same `credentialId` (credentials are scoped by `userId` in the lookup), so the claim that it wipes “cached rows for all team members” is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown formats the 'Last updated' timestamp with a hardcoded new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { dateStyle: 'short', timeStyle: 'short' }) instead of the locale already provided by useLocale(), so non-US-locale users get US date/time ordering in an otherwise localized UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, the timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`, which is hardcoded to US formatting even though the component already uses `useLocale()` for localized strings. This creates a locale/UX inconsistency for non-US users, but it’s not a functional correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses BSD/macOS-only sed -i '' syntax; on GNU/Linux sed interprets '' as an (empty) script and the command errors out, leaving a broken env update after the tunnel is already up (dev-only tooling, but a real portability bug).

adjudication.rationale: The new script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` uses `sed -i '' -E ...` to update the env file. This `-i ''` form is the macOS/BSD sed convention for “no backup”; GNU sed expects the optional suffix to be attached (e.g. `-i''` or just `-i`) and will treat `''` as a separate argument (script/filename), causing the command to fail on Linux and preventing the env update after starting the tunnel.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache handler bypasses the ICalendarCacheRepository abstraction by calling prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly instead of deleteManyByCredential, so with a Redis-backed repository active, Redis-resident cache entries survive deletion and stale data keeps being served while the user sees a 'Cache deleted successfully' toast (silent-pass), and the calendar-cache feature-disabled flag is ignored

adjudication.rationale: The new `deleteCache` TRPC handler (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`) deletes cache rows via `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` instead of going through the existing calendar-cache abstraction (`ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential`, which has a mock implementation that no-ops when the feature is disabled). This is a concrete, diff-grounded architecture/inconsistency issue that could lead to divergent behavior across implementations/feature-flag states, but the specific claim about a Redis-backed repository and stale Redis entries cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars status handler instantiates the concrete new CalendarCacheRepository() instead of resolving it through the app's repository factory, leaving the newly added CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds method as unreachable dead code and allowing the 'Last updated' status to be read from the wrong backend (DB CalendarCache table instead of the active Redis cache), including still issuing a DB groupBy when calendar-cache is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the code explicitly imports and instantiates the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` (`const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();`) and then calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which in the real repository performs a Prisma `calendarCache.groupBy` DB query. The diff also adds `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` that logs “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”, implying there is (elsewhere) a mechanism to swap in the mock when the feature is disabled. However, the diff does not show an app-wide repository factory or a Redis-backed implementation, so claims about “wrong backend”/Redis cannot be strictly verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unconditional SelectedCalendar.updatedAt write on the getAvailability hot path: the empty data {} relies on implicit Prisma @updatedAt injection (fragile, could silently become a no-op or throw), every availability check issues an O(org-size) UPDATE causing row-lock contention on delegation credentials, the write lacks try/catch error isolation so its failure fails the entire getAvailability call, nothing in the PR consumes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, and it is placed outside the fetch branch so updatedAt can be bumped without a fetch having occurred

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional write on the GoogleCalendarService availability flow: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts`, placed after the fetch/cache block, so it will run even when availability data wasn’t fetched (e.g., served from cache). This issues an `updateMany` over all `SelectedCalendar` rows for the credential on every call (potential hot-path performance/locking concern) and passes an empty `data: {}` object, implicitly relying on Prisma/`@updatedAt` semantics rather than explicitly updating a field; there’s also no error isolation (any thrown error would fail the availability call). The PR’s new UI/logic consumes `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (`cacheUpdatedAt`), not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache is an unthrottled authedProcedure that flushes all cache rows for a credential with no rate limiting or cooldown, so repeated deletion turns every incoming availability check into a cache miss and a burst of upstream Google API calls — a cheap self-inflicted DoS lever that burns Google API quota and degrades the user's own booking pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` TRPC mutation (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx`) implemented by `deleteCache.handler.ts`, which unconditionally `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` for any credential owned by the authed user. There is no rate limiting, cooldown, or other guard against repeated calls. While the downstream impact (increased cache misses leading to more upstream Google API calls) depends on caching behavior outside this diff, the lack of throttling on a cache-flush endpoint is a concrete, diff-grounded concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache ownership check uses findFirst({ id, userId }) only, so team-owned credentials (userId null, teamId set) always fail — with a plain throw new Error misclassified as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, polluting error logs — while CredentialActionsDropdown offers the delete action without ownership awareness, promising an action that can never succeed

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the credential lookup is `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`. Any credential that is not directly owned by the user (e.g., `userId` is null / shared/team-owned) will never pass this check, so `deleteCache` will always fail for those credentials. The handler then does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`, which in tRPC typically surfaces as an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` rather than a 404/403. On the client, `CredentialActionsDropdown` shows the delete-cache action purely based on `integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` and `cacheUpdatedAt` (`hasCache`), with no ownership/permission gating, so it can present an action that the server will reject for non-user-owned credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, the cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`, which hardcodes the locale to US English. Since the component already has access to `useLocale()` (`const { t } = useLocale();`), this introduces user-visible incorrect date formatting for non-US locales (and potentially mismatched expectations for locale-specific date formats) in the new cache status UI.
